properties.description:
PROJECT SCOPE

Provide one new dedicated AFCI/GFCI protected 20A 120V branch circuit from the main panel on the exterior wall of the house to a new kitchen range hood.
No meter work being performed.

INSTALLATION DETAILS

Install a vertical 1-inch Steel EMT raceway exiting the main electrical panel from a 1-inch LR conduit body (located below all energized parts) on the homes exterior brick wall. Transition raceway to horizontal orientation for building penetration using a 1 LB. Penetrate into the accessible attic with 1 EMT terminating into a 4-11/16 steel junction box with a blank cover.

Install #10-2 UF-B cable (1 HOT 1 NEUTRAL 1 EGC) (Sunlight Resistant/Wet Location rated) from the range hood to the steel junction box. Cable will be routed along ceiling rafters; any portion below 7 will be protected by guard strips per NEC 320.23. The #10-2 UF-B will be sleeved continuously from the 4-11/16 junction box through the LB down the vertical EMT and through the LR terminating directly into the main panel . This avoids all splices providing a continuous run from the OCPD to the appliance.

CODE COMPLIANCE NOTES:

10 AWG conductors are specd. for this 20A circuit to account for ambient temperature correction in the unconditioned attic and sun-exposed exterior raceway. The EMT will be sealed with duct seal at the attic box and panel entry to prevent moisture migration and condensation per NEC 300.7. All cables and raceways will be supported/secured per NEC. All exterior fittings/hardware will be UL-listed rain-tight compression type. All cables and raceways will be supported and secured per NEC requirements. An insulated throat fitting or plastic bushing will be used at all EMT entry points to protect the cable jacket from abrasion. All wire terminations will be torqued to the manufacturer specifications per 2023 NEC 110.14(D)

properties.description:
Replacing cast iron pipes with pvc pipes and running a main building sewer line to the city.

Per contractor agent 
The project involves replacing an aging cast iron plumbing system located beneath the home by tunneling under the foundation. This method allows access to the existing sewer lines without the need to disturb or remove interior flooring. A tunnel will be carefully excavated beneath the structure to expose the old cast iron pipes which have likely deteriorated over time due to corrosion scaling and potential cracking.
Once exposed the outdated cast iron piping will be removed and replaced with new durable PVC piping. PVC (polyvinyl chloride) is resistant to corrosion has a longer lifespan and provides improved flow efficiency compared to cast iron. The new system will be installed to meet current plumbing codes and ensure reliable wastewater drainage.
In addition the property will be transitioned from an outdated backyard septic system to the municipal sewer system. This will involve connecting the new PVC plumbing to the city sewer line ensuring proper alignment grading and compliance with local regulations. The septic system will be properly abandoned according to code. This upgrade will provide a more efficient low-maintenance and environmentally compliant wastewater solution for the home. 
The job will take place in the front side of the house and underneath.

properties.description:
Diagnostic revealed a leak on the tub drain for unit C and a belly on the main drain under unit C bathroom.

- Plan of action is to apply for a permit with the customers jurisdiction to legally and professionally proceed with repairs. 
- Begin by excavating the entry hole at the back of the building outside of unit C.
- Then tunnel underneath the foundation of the building approximately 10 feet to access and expose noted diagnostic issues. 
- If additional tunneling or beam penetration is needed a supplemented estimate will be provided. 
- If any more work is needed such as solid rock removal roots or any unforeseeable objects come across this estimate will be supplemented to accommodate the additional work needed to complete the job. 
- Defective drains will be removed from the plumbing system and debris will be hauled away. - Drains will then be replaced with new DWV schedule 40 PVC pipe and fittings in accordance with plumbing code. 
- Pipe will be well supported and strapped to underneath foundation to prevent the same thing happening in the future. 
- After work is completed we will then perform a static test on the entire drain system to ensure there are no further leaks. If additional leaks are found a separate estimate will be presented for the repair.

properties.description:
We will be removing the existing failing grease interceptor and installing a new codecompliant grease trap in the same general location. Work includes excavation demolition of the existing interceptor installation of new piping connections setting the new interceptor and restoring the work area to grade.
Detailed Scope:

Excavate to expose the existing grease trap and associated inlet/outlet piping.
Disconnect and remove the existing grease interceptor including damaged or noncompliant piping sections.
Install a new (Cityapproved) grease interceptor sized per fixture count and City of Austin Industrial Waste requirements.
Set the new unit on a properly compacted and leveled base.
Reconnect all inlet and outlet plumbing using approved materials and fittings.
Install new cleanouts as required by current code.
Ensure proper flow line elevations and venting per Austin Water and UPC/IPC requirements.
Backfill and compact the excavation area; restore concrete/asphalt or surface material as needed.
Perform final testing for watertightness flow and proper operation.
Submit required SAWS/Industrial Waste documentation including asbuilt information and fixture count verification.

No changes to existing building water distribution or sewer layout beyond the grease trap connections.
All work will comply with City of Austin Plumbing Code Industrial Waste regulations and Whataburger operational safety requirements.
